identity.title: Bound Workbench run-log memory without losing OVLog evidence

origin.kind: master-backlog maintenance priority and user-approved continuation
origin.summary: The Workbench session RunLog is an unbounded in-memory projection even though every current AppendLog call also routes to the existing durable rolling OVLog files.

state.current_summary: Workbench now keeps the newest 3,000 session entries in newest-first order after routing every event to rolling OVLog files; the operator-facing boundary is localized, all local and documentation gates pass, and hosted CI #76 succeeded.

objective.summary: Keep the newest 3,000 Workbench session entries in memory while every event remains routed to durable OVLog files and the operator can distinguish the two retention surfaces.
constraints: Do not change Preview, Publish, Run, Validation, recipe, or source/result behavior.
Do not change the existing 50 MB by 20-backup rolling-file policy or add a new export format.
Keep the policy with the Workbench ViewModel owner and reuse the existing Application Log surface.

criteria.text: RunLog never exceeds 3,000 entries through the production AppendLog path and retains the newest entries in newest-first order.
Entries pruned from the in-memory Workbench projection remain present in the flushed OVLog ALL file.
The localized Application Log caption states the bounded memory view and complete rolling-file boundary without starting or changing recipe execution.
Focused regression, Debug/Release builds, structure checks, current-build Wide/Compact English/Korean UI evidence, refreshed fixed R0 inputs, documentation checks, and hosted CI pass.

context.summary: AppendLog owns the sole current RunLog insertion path and OVLog routing.
The linked Session Log pane presents bounded Application Log and Workbench Session projections.

artifacts.summary: Current-build before/after screenshots, capture-quality reports, focused retention and OVLog verification, builds, and R0 validation output.

evidence.observation: AppendLog inserts into Workbench RunLog without a cap and writes the same event to OVLog. The existing Application Log projection already caps memory at 3,000 entries, while log4net rolls durable ALL files at 50 MB with 20 backups. Fresh current-Release Wide 1920x1040 and Compact 1280x760 Session Log baselines passed capture-quality checks on the dynamically selected leftmost monitor.

The current Release verifier passed 6/6: RunLog stayed at 3,000 newest-first entries after 3,002 production AppendLog calls, the two pruned entries and all generated entries remained in the flushed OVLog ALL file, English/Korean retention text matched the contract, and recipe/execution state did not change.
